item.title: It's a Fact
item.description: My Cousin Vinny is the courtroom comedy in which recently licensed New York attorney, Vincent Gambini, is called on to defend his cousin and cousin's friend in a murder trial in Alabama. Definitely among the movies I've seen the most in my life, and in spite of that, i still find myself laughing out loud throughout the film. Everything in this film hits and, though some moments are products of the time, it still feels pretty evergreen. Where do I start? I think it has to be the screenplay. I never realized this movie was two hours. It just moves and paces itself perfectly. It never feels like there's a lull, and it also does a really good job of building real dramatic tension. Using the trial to take us through the twists and turns along with the legal defense. Marissa Tomei's performance is outstanding. Her chemistry with Pesci shines on screen, they have a terrific rapport with each other. Pesci himself shows that, though most of his career is in supporting roles, he really can carry a lead role. And it was nice to see that pretty much all of the ensemble got a moment. Some kind of bit or punchline to round out the comedy. 10/10 This movie is so good that it's been cited by actual lawyers about how to cross examine witnesses. The hard cuts to hit a punchline had me rolling. Example "It's a word that comes from merry old England, and all our little ancestors" (Hard cuts to two black jurors). There's just enough scenery chewing to be entertaining and not quite over the top. Just a fantastic movie.

item.description: Chicago’s latest internet project apparently requires everyone to give a very large bean a nudge. A viral flyer is inviting people to gather at Cloud Gate and move the sculpture seven inches to the left. The advertised appointment is November 8 at the oddly specific time of 12:47 p.m. There is one obvious complication: the Bean weighs about 110 tons. Created by artist Anish Kapoor, the polished stainless steel landmark sits in Millennium Park and reflects the city skyline across its curved surface. Moving it is not exactly comparable to rearranging the living room. Online discussion treats the invitation as another wonderfully absurd community joke. The circulating post does not establish that the city approved a relocation, that an organised attempt will happen, or that anything has actually moved. For now, the confirmed attraction is the ridiculous premise. Apparently, even one of Chicago’s most famous landmarks could use better positioning.
